Overnight White Bread Baker's Percentage

One loaf from a night in the refrigerator. Yeast stays very low, and you bake the next day only after the chill has left the dough.

Detailed method

One loaf, mixed today and baked tomorrow. Currently 500 g flour, 72% hydration, 2% salt, and 0.25% yeast. That is 360 g water, 10 g salt, and 1.3 g yeast, 871.3 g of dough. Currently 1 loaf of 871.3 g. The small yeast amount is for a night in the refrigerator. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 360 g water, 10 g salt, and 1.3 g instant yeast until no dry flour remains. At 72% the dough is soft. Knead 6 to 8 minutes, until smooth. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Rest Cover the bowl for 30 minutes at about 24°C (75°F). With 0.25% yeast it will barely puff.
  3. Cold Refrigerate the covered dough at about 4°C (39°F) for 12 to 16 hours. It should grow by about half overnight, not spill over the bowl.
  4. Warm Take it out and leave it covered for 45 to 70 minutes, until it is no longer cold in the middle. The full dough is 871.3 g, one loaf.
  5. Shape Tighten it into one oval and set it seam-side down on a floured cloth, or in a greased tin. The default 871.3 g uses a loaf pan about 23 cm long, 13 cm wide, and 7 cm high. If you change the amount, use a pan sized to fit, or split the dough. This batch is 1 loaf.
  6. Proof Cover the shaped loaf for 45 to 75 minutes, until it has grown by about half and a finger press springs back slowly. With 0.25% yeast this last rise is slower than a same-day dough.
  7. Bake Heat the oven to 220°C (430°F). Score once. Bake 20 minutes with steam, then 15 to 20 minutes at 200°C (390°F), until the crust is golden and the sides are firm. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
